validity.recommendation: check LengthKnown -- two independent, more-current sources put PG&E's backbone/local gas transmission system materially below the recorded 7,000 mi
validity.researcher_notes: The sheet's existing ref (pge.com/gas-systems/pipeline.html) DOES state the recorded value verbatim ('PG&E's nearly 7,000 miles of gas transmission pipelines') and names the pipeline, so that unit re-verifies clean on its own terms (see the Length fill below). But casting a wider net for the required second independent source surfaced a material disagreement: (1) PHMSA's own 'PG&E System Overview' safety page states PG&E 'operates nearly 5,700 miles of gas transmission pipelines' (Wayback capture 2025-01-02); (2) PG&E Corp's 2025 Corporate Sustainability Report 'About PG&E' page states '5,650 miles of backbone and local gas transmission pipelines' (current, dated 2025); (3) PG&E Corp's FY2023 10-K (SEC EDGAR, filed 2024, describing the system as of 2023-12-31) states 'over 6,400 miles of backbone and local transmission pipelines'. PHMSA (an independent federal regulator) and PG&E's own 2025 CSR agree within rounding at ~5,650-5,700 mi -- two independent origins pointing to a figure roughly 19-20% below the sheet's 7,000. The SEC 10-K's 6,400 (as of end-2023) sits between the two. The pge.com marketing page carrying the sheet's 7,000 figure is undated and may describe a broader definition (e.g. including some distribution-adjacent or historical mileage) or simply be stale copy. Recommend the researcher weigh 5,650-5,700 (PHMSA + 2025 CSR, the two most current, most precisely-dated, mutually-corroborating figures) against the sheet's 7,000 and update LengthKnown accordingly; candidate value given as 5650 (2025 CSR, most recent).

validity.recommendation: note what the recorded Diameter represents -- one backbone line's pipe size, not a single system-wide figure
validity.researcher_notes: Per the scope guidance for utility-system rows (P6233/P6250): a single Diameter value on a 7,000-mile, multi-line system is the largest/most-cited line at best, not a literal system-wide constant. The recorded 30 in traces to the NTSB investigation of the 2010 San Bruno rupture on PG&E's Line 132, a 30-inch-diameter intrastate transmission segment (confirmed via the Pipeline Safety Trust page, Wayback capture, since the live page 403s bot traffic -- see the Diameter fill). I did not find a documented larger backbone diameter to supersede it (no diameter figures surfaced in PG&E's SEC filings or CSR), so 30 in stands as the best-documented single figure, understood to represent one prominent line rather than a verified system-wide maximum.

fills.researcher_notes: Confirmed as a transmission system (not gathering/distribution) by two independent sources; correctly classified.

This is a whole-system row (PG&E's backbone + local gas transmission network), not a single certificated project, so there is no one 'proposal' event/date to source -- the network was built up incrementally across decades (documented interstate interconnection expansions alone span at least 1998-2002 per the EIA workbook's historical sheet, and the intrastate backbone predates that by decades). Searched PG&E's gas-system pages, PG&E Corp's 2023 10-K and 2025 CSR, and the PHMSA system-overview page -- none give a founding/proposal date for the system as a whole. Leaving ProposalYear UNRESOLVED rather than force a single year onto a system built over a century.

Same system-vs-project problem as Proposal: no single construction-start date applies to a network built and expanded continuously since the early-to-mid 20th century. Searched the same source set (pge.com, PG&E Corp SEC filings/CSR, PHMSA) with no system-wide construction-start date found. UNRESOLVED rather than fabricated.

Same system-vs-project limitation: PG&E's gas transmission backbone has been in continuous operation and expansion for decades with no single in-service year. The EIA historical-projects sheet documents individual PG&E gas-transmission expansions going back to at least the 1990s-2000s (e.g. 'PG&E-NW Mainline Expansion', in service 1998; 'PG&E Redwood Path', in service 2002) but these are discrete expansion PROJECTS, not the system's founding date, and per the EIA system-vs-project rule (ADDENDUM failure mode 2) none of them can stand in for this system row's StartYear1. Searched pge.com, PG&E Corp SEC filings/CSR, and PHMSA for a system-wide start date; none given. UNRESOLVED.

No single system-wide throughput/design-capacity figure found. Checked pge.com's gas-system pages, PG&E Corp's 2023 10-K and 2025 CSR (both give mileage, not capacity), the PHMSA system-overview page, and the EIA workbook (which -- per the EIA system-vs-project rule -- only carries per-project 'Additional Capacity' for discrete expansions, not an aggregate system figure, and this row is the system, not a project). Left blank rather than substituting a project-level or aggregated proxy number.

MAOP varies line-by-line across a 7,000-mile system of many vintages and diameters (this is precisely the defect that caused the San Bruno rupture -- inconsistent, poorly documented pressure history on Line 132 alone). No single system-wide operating pressure is stated in PG&E's public materials, its SEC filings, or the PHMSA page I reviewed. Left blank rather than force a single-line figure onto the whole system.
